artists.biography:
Jem Godfrey began in music as a songwriter for many pop and mainstream groups. In fact, he’s written four number one singles in the UK for groups such as Atomic Kitten and Shayne Ward. In 2004, he began the group FROST* in England and ventured into the realm of progressive rock. For his debut album, called “Milliontown”, Jem enlisted guitarist John Mitchell (Arena, Kino), bassist John Jowitt (IQ, Jadis), and drummer Andy Edwards (IQ). The album itself is a mixture of neo progressive rock, progressive metal undertones, some symphonic leanings, and some more mainstream ideals. “Milliontown” was released on July 18th 2006 in the USA and July 24th in the UK. FROST* is a band to look out for in the future and they seem to have a long, fruitful future ahead of them.

A second album titled “Experiments in Mass Appeal” was released in November 2008. Declan Burke from (Darwin’s Radio) has been added to the lineup for additional guitar and to take up lead vocals.

perplexity.description:
Frost's Life in the Wires, released in 2024 via InsideOutMusic (Sony Music), is a double concept album that stands as one of the most ambitious entries in the UK neo-prog band's discography. Clocking in at nearly 90 minutes across 14 tracks, the album showcases Frost's signature blend of melodic rock, intricate keyboard textures, and dynamic guitar work, anchored by the talents of Jem Godfrey, John Mitchell, Nathan King, and Craig Blundell. The music traverses atmospheric soundscapes, driving rhythms, and emotive vocal performances, reflecting the band's evolution while staying rooted in the progressive rock tradition.

Life in the Wires is notable for its conceptual depth and expansive songwriting, marking a creative high point for Frost and further solidifying their reputation in the modern prog scene. The album received positive critical attention for its ambitious scope, cohesive narrative, and technical proficiency, with reviewers highlighting its thematic resonance and musical craftsmanship. As Frost's latest studio release, it demonstrates both continuity with their established sound and a willingness to push boundaries, earning praise from fans and critics alike within the progressive rock community.
